brief: Goldman's Financials desk describes three cross-currents driving intraday trading: agentic AI risk to consumer-facing businesses, Fed hikes with a flatter curve, and election chatter, with agentic risk the primary focus. Investors are pricing risk that AI agents narrow companies' ability to monetize consumers, hitting personal insurance (ALL, PGR, TRV), small-cap insurance lead generators (down high-single to low-double-digit percent), insurance broker GSHD, and wealth managers and retail brokers (SCHW, AMP, RJF). Small- and mid-cap banks outperform large banks because they carry less fee and wealth-management business and more commercial deposits. In payments, late-morning underperformance in Visa and Mastercard is debated as flow-of-funds selling versus wallet-integration risk from a PayPal partnership, with most feedback favoring flow-of-funds. By afternoon investors turn broadly defensive: CBRE and JLL underperform peers by about 2%, large liquid defensive names such as JPMorgan and Visa trade heavy, and exchanges see choppy underperformance despite no direct agentic read-through. Goldman calls this an uncertainty discount as investors work through fundamentals, noting past AI-driven choppy tapes rewarded patience over day-one defense. A trader, Mitola, reports high volumes, rising thematic trading, and a complete buyers' strike with no dip-buying, similar to prior episodes this year.
